target:
The staging reminder was flagging `git commit -m"add export handler"` as a stage-all. I fixed it and committed the fix as `3f575a4`.

**Cause:** `stages_all` in `src/staging.py` scanned every letter of a short-option cluster. Shell splitting turns `-m"add export handler"` into the single word `-madd export handler`. The scan found the `a` in "add" and read it as `-a`, which stages everything. The `a` in "handler" would have matched the same way.

**Fix:** The scan now stops at a value-taking option (`-m`, `-F`, `-c`, `-C`, `-t`), since the letters after it are its value. When the value is a separate word, that word is skipped, so `-m '--all'` is no longer flagged.

**Tests:** I added two test cases to `tests/test_staging.py`:
- Letters inside a message do not trigger the reminder, covering the reported command plus `-m 'add all the things'`, `-m -a`, `-m '--all'` and `-ma 'add'`.
- A stage-all flag after a message still triggers it, covering `-m "fix" -a` and `-m'fix' --all`.

All 7 tests pass, and the reported command now returns `False`.

**Commit:** Only `src/staging.py` and `tests/test_staging.py` are in the commit. I left out the existing `README.md` edit and the untracked `notes/` folder because they aren't part of this fix.
